title: Multi-zone, light-driven landscape post-processing in Photoshop (Part 2 CR images week 2)
summary: The video demonstrates a practical, artistically driven post-processing workflow for winter landscape images using a pared-down toolset in Photoshop and Camera Raw. Central ideas include (1) choosing and prioritizing images quickly, (2) treating a scene as multiple zones (sky, mid-ground, foreground) to preserve detail across extreme tonal ranges, (3) building up an image through iterative RAW adjustments and selective color work, and (4) using a small set of tools in a fluid, painterly workflow rather than a traditional layered or plugin-heavy approach. The presenter emphasizes entering an artistic state rather than becoming overwhelmed by technical options, and shows how to combine RAW edits, selective painting, fog/diffusion, and perspective warps to craft a cohesive, three- to four-zone composition with a strong focal point and atmospheric depth. Throughout, he contrasts a minimal-tool philosophy with ambitious image-building steps, including sky restoration, hard-edged light on mountains, and fog/drift to create mood and depth.

sections.description: The presenter notes the need to quickly pick usable images and introduces the idea that some shots are best processed as distinct zones (sky, mid-ground, foreground) to manage tonal contrast.

sections.description: He argues for a painterly approach and a limited toolset, describing how he learned to work without relying on layers, and emphasizes staying in an artistic state rather than chasing every new technique.

sections.title: Three-zone editing concept and initial sky treatment
concepts: three-zone shot analysis (sky, trees, foreground)
dark sky to drive eye toward light
initial RAW adjustments to restore natural dynamic range
sections.description: The workflow is framed around a three-zone composition. The sky is darkened to push light upward, and dynamic range is adjusted to resemble the eye’s view while preserving detail in trees and foreground.

sections.title: History-driven edits and selective painting workflow

non-layer painting across the image

sections.description: The video demonstrates using the History Brush to selectively apply earlier edits, effectively painting adjustments onto the image without creating many layers. The presenter notes a dislike for focus stacking and emphasizes a fluid, history-driven approach to painting light and color.

sections.title: Perspective Warp and composition refinements
concepts: Perspective Warp as a starting point for composition

leading lines and cloud convergence toward the focal point
sections.description: A shift in emphasis toward composition tools—perspective warp, trapezoid-based warping, and leading lines—to improve cloud convergence on the mountain and to align the shot with a stronger compositional framework.

sections.title: Color control, light on the mountain, and atmospheric fog in multi-zone processing
concepts: color grading and camera calibration for cohesive sky tones
selective color adjustments
fog/diffusion painting to add atmosphere
clone-painting across images to composite light
final touch workflow (raw vs. Photoshop) with multiple passes
sections.description: This section covers crafting light on the mountain through painting with light and iterative color work, employing color grading, selective color, and camera calibration to achieve consistent skies. Fog and diffusion are painted in for depth, with cross-image painting (clone-paint) and multiple RAW/PS passes to unify tone and atmosphere. The section culminates with a multi-pass approach to a four-zone-like result, balancing sky, mid-ground, and foreground light and texture.
